definition: A digital identity model where individuals control their personal data and credentials without relying on centralized authorities like governments or corporations.
metaDescription: Learn about self-sovereign identity - a privacy-focused approach to digital identity that gives users complete control over their personal data.
simpleExplanation: Think of it like having a digital wallet that contains all your identity documents, but only you control what information to share and with whom. Instead of Facebook or Google managing your identity, you own and manage it yourself.
whyItMatters: It eliminates the need to trust third parties with your personal information, reduces data breaches, and gives you complete control over your digital identity. You can prove who you are without exposing unnecessary personal details.
technicalDetail: Uses blockchain or distributed ledger technology to create tamper-proof digital credentials. Private keys enable cryptographic proof of identity ownership, while verifiable credentials can be selectively disclosed. The system operates on decentralized identifiers (DIDs) that don't require central registration authorities.

examples.explanation: You store your driver's license as a digital credential on your phone. When buying alcohol, you can prove you're over 21 without revealing your exact birthdate, address, or license number.
Your university issues you a digital diploma that you control. You can instantly prove your degree to employers without contacting the university or sharing transcripts through third-party services.
Instead of uploading ID photos to websites, you can cryptographically prove you meet age requirements without revealing your identity, birthdate, or other personal information.
